citation: Stasinaki AN, Zaras N, Methenitis S, Tsitkanou S, Krase A, Kavvoura A, Terzis G. Triceps Brachii Muscle Strength and Architectural Adaptations with Resistance Training Exercises at Short or Long Fascicle Length. J Funct Morphol Kinesiol. 2018;3(2):28
design: Within-subject training study (one arm per exercise)
intervention_comparison: Unilateral cable push-down (triceps short) vs unilateral cable overhead extension with the other arm (triceps long), 6 sets x 6RM
outcome_measure: Ultrasound triceps thickness at 50% and 60% of arm length; long-head longitudinal area; fascicle angle and length; elbow-extension 1RM
result_effect_uncertainty: Thickness at 50%: +10.7 +/- 15.3% (push-down) vs +13.7 +/- 9.0% (overhead); at 60%: +15.5 +/- 18.8% vs +19.4 +/- 16.3%. 1RM +40.1 +/- 21.3% vs +44.5 +/- 20.1%. citation: Goto M, Maeda C, Hirayama T, Terada S, Nirengi S, Kurosawa Y, Nagano A, Hamaoka T. Partial Range of Motion Exercise Is Effective for Facilitating Muscle Hypertrophy and Function Through Sustained Intramuscular Hypoxia in Young Trained Men. J Strength Cond Res. 2019;33(5):1286-1294

citation: Sato S, Yoshida R, Kiyono R, Yahata K, Yasaka K, Nunes JP, Nosaka K, Nakamura M. Elbow Joint Angles in Elbow Flexor Unilateral Resistance Exercise Training Determine Its Effects on Muscle Strength and Thickness of Trained and Non-trained Arms. Front Physiol. 2021;12:734509

intervention_comparison: Seated dumbbell preacher curl (shoulder flexed 45 degrees, forearm supinated) in the bottom range 0-50 degrees of elbow flexion vs the top range 80-130 degrees; 3 x 10
outcome_measure: Ultrasound thickness of biceps brachii + brachialis; isometric, concentric and eccentric elbow-flexion torque; cross-education to the other arm

citation: Gschneidner D, Carlson L, Steele J, Fisher JP. The effects of lengthened-partial range of motion resistance training of the limbs on arm and thigh muscle area: A multi-site randomised trial. J Sports Sci. 2025;43(23):2963-2976
